chunks: God: There is no god but He, the Lord of the glorious throne.

key_terms.إِلَٰهَ: God or deity, referring to the object of worship.
key_terms.الرَّبُّ: Lord, Master, or Sustainer, implying ownership and care.
key_terms.اللَّهُ: The specific name of God, often used to denote the unique deity.
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: The Throne, symbolizing God's supreme authority and dominion over creation.
key_terms.الْعَظِيمِ: The Great, an attribute emphasizing the magnitude and majesty of the Throne or God.

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Lord of the Great Throne' signify in Islamic theology?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of Tawhid al-Rububiyyah, affirming Allah's absolute dominion over the cosmos, symbolized by the 'Great Throne' (Al-Arsh). It serves as a powerful declaration of monotheism that underscores God's transcendence and unique authority, resonating with the Shia emphasis on divine unity and sovereignty in both theological and spiritual contexts.
